CHROMIUM: arm64: dts: qcom: sdm845-cheza: Add RPMh VRM/XOB regulators Add regulator devices for PMIC regulators managed via VRM and XOB RPMh accelerators. A few notes here: - Regulators are added directly to the board file. While it's true that this will mean a bunch of copy/pasting for other boards that are very similar, this is probably the right call since boards could make changes to the way these regulators are hooked up and trying to find a way to avoid duplication will result in some confusing node overrides. - Regulators that are hooked up to supply pins on the SoC are given an alias matching the name of that pin (pin name comes from the Qualcomm SoC "device specification" doc). - Other regulator labels are based on the schematic. If there is more than one logical name on the schematic for the same rail the secondary names are also listed and should be referred to as appropriate. - Regulators all default to HPM mode w/ no ability to switch modes. Future patches can switch things to LPM and possibly add dynamic load switching if we have determined there's a benefit. This should only be done for rails where we'll actually be able to take advantage of the lower power modes so we don't need to churn with lots of patches adding regulator_set_load() calls to drivers. NOTE: This patch is loosely based on one originally shared to me by David Collins for sdm845-mtp. BUG=b:74988960 TEST=Regulators seem to be getting set Change-Id: I3da35f6fdb89d1a81d1f64f0b151453731478b02 Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1042996 Reviewed-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org>

vm_tools: seneschal: Use full path for share destination Use the full source path rather than just the basename when calculating the destination of a SharePath request. "Downloads/foo/bar" will now appear as "/Downloads/foo/bar" instead of just "/bar". This means that it is now possible to share 2 paths with the same basename but different ancestors. However, ancestor directories are not writable unless they are explicitly shared as well. Additionally, some remove operations may return -EBUSY. For example, if a user shares "Downloads/foo/bar" and then later shares "Downloads/foo", attempting to remove "Downloads/foo/bar" will return -EBUSY since it is still bind mounted. BUG=chromium:703939 TEST=manual Sharing a nested directory followed by sharing one of its ancestors works. Similarly, sharing a directory and then later sharing one of its children also works. Ancestor directories that have not been shared are not writable and return -EPERM. Can currently be tested in crosh by running `vmc share <vm> <path in downloads>`.
